STATEMENT OF OBJ,ECTS AND REASONS 
The Chaparmukh-Silghst Railway Company Limited and the 
Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Company Limited are owners respectively 
of the Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Line and the Katakhal-Lalabazar 
Railway Line which are at present being worked and managed by the 
North-East Frontier Railway, in accordance with the working agree-
ments. As the assets of these two Companies are not eftlcientiy main-
tained and the Companies are not in a position to rehabilitate them, it 
has beeome necessary to acquire the undertakings f1l the Companies 
in relation to the aforesaid railway lines for the purpose of continuance 
of operation of these two lines 'which is of vital import811ce to the remote 
North-Eas~em areas of the country and to protect the liBks of eom-
'munkation between the said areas and the rest of the country.

Clause 6(1) of the Bill provides 'for the payment, in cash, an

2. Clause 7 provides for payment of simple interest on the amounts 
specified in clause 6 (1), reduced by the amounts due to the Centl'Jll

MEMORANDUM REGARDING DELEGATED LEGISLATION 
Clause 15 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to make 
rules to carry out the provisions of the Act. ThO'Ugh there is no specific 
provision in the Bill which would require the making of rules. it may 
not be possible to rule out altogether any contingency that may arise 
in future which might necessitate the making of rules. Hence, as a 
matter of abundant caution, clause 15 has been incorporated in the 
Bill. 
2. Clause 16 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to remove 
by order any difficulty which may arise in giving effect to the provisions 
of the Act. This is by way of abundant caution and for covering difficul-
ties which it is not practicable to visualise. 
3. As the matters with respect of which rules may be made under 
clause 15 pertain to matters of proc~dure or detail and as the matters 
with respect to which orders may be made under clause 16 pertain to 
matters which it is not practicable to visualise at this stage, the dele-
gation of legislative power is of a normal character.
